description: Context: This PR implements the first wave of cost-optimization automation: an autotune controller that suggests and gradually applies default batching/caching parameters, a quantization profile registry with runtime selection heuristics, and a unit-economics simulation + tooling surface in the Console. Motivation: customers running large inference workloads need predictable unit economics; manually tuning batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization across routes is error-prone. Autotune reduces operational overhead and consistently improves token-level cost without manual intervention. What changed (summary): - Autotune controller (service/autotune/controller.py): periodic analysis job that consumes sampling metrics (latency, tokens-per-request, seq-dist) and proposes safe default overrides for per-route batching and caching. Includes canary rollout logic (canary_fraction, metric_watchers) and automatic fallback when error/latency regressions exceed thresholds. - Scheduler/cost model (runtime/scheduler/cost_model.py): integrates estimated prefix-cache hit-rate and batching improvement into cost function used by autotune to score proposals. - Prefix cache improvements (runtime/cache/prefix_cache.py): exposes hit-rate histograms and TTL-aware eviction hints used by the autotune scoring model. - Quantization profiles (models/quant_profiles/*.yaml): new profile registry (aes/4bit, aes/3bit, fp16 variants) and heuristics to pick profiles based on SLO, sequence length distribution, and observed perplexity/regression checks. New safe-fallback path re-runs 10-sample evals on old profile for validation. - Unit economics tooling (webapp/src/components/UnitEconSimulator.tsx + webapp/src/api/unit_econ.ts): interactive simulator to model cost/latency/quality tradeoffs given workload characteristics; backend endpoints to run short simulations and persist experiment configs. - SDK bindings (sdk/python/redwood/optimize.py, sdk/typescript/src/optimizeClient.ts): expose APIs to fetch autotune proposals and trigger manual apply/rollback. - Tests: integration/e2e tests to validate canary rollout, fallback behavior, and quant profile safety checks. Motivation/Design notes: - Conservative-by-default: proposals are ranked by expected cost savings and risk; autotune only applies changes that meet a minimum expected improvement and have a low risk score. - Canary + watch windows: we apply changes to a small fraction (default 5%) and monitor latency, error rate, and model quality regression signals for 30 minutes before scaling up. - Quality checks: quant profile switches run a mini-eval harness on recent user prompts (10 examples) to detect obvious quality regressions, with manual approval required if regression crosses threshold. - Unit-econ simulator: mirrors our internal unit economics model (tokens, batching efficiency, GPU occupancy assumptions) so customers can reason about expected savings before applying. Checklist: - [x] Autotune controller implementation - [x] Canary rollouts + automatic fallback - [x] Quant profile registry + heuristic selection - [x] Unit-econ simulator UI + persistence - [x] SDK endpoints and docs - [x] Integration tests (canary + fallback) - [x] Docs and runbook (docs/engineering/autotune.md) Performance impact (measured in CI staging and internal perf lab): - Average token cost reduced by 18-25% for text-generation workloads tested (median ~22%) depending on sequence-length mix. - 95th percentile latency increased by <=5% in the worst-case canary; we added SLO gates to prevent larger regressions. - Model quality regressions detected in <1% of profile switches; those are automatically flagged and rolled back. Migration/upgrade notes: - Autotune is off by default; operators can opt-in per-organization or per-route. - Config knobs: autotune.enabled, autotune.canary_fraction, autotune.min_expected_savings, autotune.risk_threshold. - Rollback is a single-checkbox in Console and via SDK: applyRollback(route_id). Docs and runbook: docs/engineering/autotune.md includes troubleshooting steps, incident checklist, and performance validation steps. CI and validation: - CI pipeline updated to include autotune integration test matrix (ci/ci-autotune.yaml). One e2e run flaked on first attempt against staging (timing-dependent) but requeued and passed; added stronger synchronization to avoid flakiness. Risks and mitigations: - Risk: overly aggressive quantization leads to quality regressions. Mitigation: mini-eval + SLO gating + manual approval for high-impact routes. - Risk: autotune thrashing settings on spiky workloads. Mitigation: hysteresis and minimum apply durations; proposals require improvement to be sustained for the watch window before expansion. Related work: ENG-7821 (autotune controller design), PM-442 (unit-econ simulator spec), SUP-3312 (customer ask: lower inference spend for batch jobs). Release notes: "Autotune: add safe defaults for batching/caching, quantization profile registry, and unit-economics simulator. Autotune is opt-in; admins can preview savings in Console." Merge outcome: PR was reviewed by Noah, Liam, Sofia, and Maya. All reviewers approved after two rounds of changes. CI passed on final run. Merged via squash on 2024-11-19.
release_notes: Autotune: add safe defaults for batching/caching, quantization profile registry, and unit-economics simulator. Opt-in feature with canary rollouts and automatic fallback; see docs/engineering/autotune.md for details.
notes_for_release: Feature is opt-in by default; enable per-org or per-route.
Admins can preview expected savings in Console before applying.
